page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.3xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9-based Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 7500 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the i8ge.3xlarge demonstrates exceptional memory performance, achieving a top-tier rating in the Passmark memory score and strong results in large-block read and write memory bandwidth. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong. However, CPU encryption performance is weak, as indicated by the Passmark encryption test. Large language model inference speeds are mixed, with weak performance in small-model text generation and medium-model prompt processing, though medium-model text generation remains average.

This instance offers high resource density, combining substantial local NVMe storage with a generous memory allocation on an energy-efficient ARM64 architecture. This makes it highly cost-efficient for data-intensive workloads that require rapid local storage access and high memory throughput without the overhead of x86 licensing. The i8ge.3xlarge is well-suited for high-throughput databases, large-scale caching layers, data indexing, and storage-heavy analytical workloads.

The i8ge.3xlarge is highly suited for storage-intensive workloads, high-throughput databases, and caching applications requiring large local storage capacities and rapid memory access.
